newsitem.title: USA: Ford may buy stadium name rights - paper.
newsitem.headline: Ford may buy stadium name rights - paper.

text.p: Ford Motor Co's board of directors is expected to announce Thursday whether to buy rights to name a proposed new downtown football stadium for the Detroit Lions, The Detroit News reported on Tuesday.
The automaker would pay $30 million to $40 million for the rights to name the domed facility, providing a major financing boost for the $225 million project, the newspaper said.

"There is nothing to announce at this time," a Ford spokesman said on Tuesday. Ford's board of directors, which includes Lions owners William Clay Ford and his son, William Clay Ford Jr., has a regular meeting scheduled on Thursday.

The Lions face a November 1 deadline to attract $50 million in corporate and private contributions to help finance the project, which would include any proceeds from the sale of name rights to the stadium.

Under plans announced last month, financing for the stadium also includes a $50 million contribution from the Lions, an $80 million bond issue backed by proposed Wayne County taxes on hotel rooms and car rentals, $20 million from the sale of surplus Wayne County land, $15 million in city of Detroit general obligation bonds and up to $30 million in bonds issued by the Detroit Downtown Development Authority.
The one percent hotel tax and two percent car rental tax are subject to approval by Wayne County voters in a referrendum on the November 5 ballot.

The Detroit News, quoting unnamed sources, said William Clay Ford and William Clay Ford Jr., two of three Ford family members on the Ford Motor Co board of directors, may abstain from any board votes on acquiring the stadium name rights.
The other Ford family member on the board, Edsel Ford II, does not own an interest in the Lions.
The Detroit Free Press also reported that Chrysler Corp was interested acquiring rights to the stadium name. A Chrysler spokeswoman was not immediately available for comment.
Mayor Dennis Archer reportedly approached Ford, Chrysler and General Motors Corp for contributions to the project within the past three weeks.
